forever.label: Summary
forever.note: BETA 17 SEP · LAUNCH 4 NOV · NO SIM OR LOG DATA EXISTS YET

foreverOutlook.why: Blizzard states Assassination now focuses on poison damage, and unified Hit/Crit explicitly covers poisons. Mutilate appeared in the BlizzCon demo. Most confirmed upside of the four.
Confirmed redirection toward bleeds and stealth effects, plus a new 16-point talent milestone. The spec that had the least to lose.
Blizzard says Combat keeps its upfront style. One-Handed Axes join the weapon list, which widens your options without changing the rotation.
No confirmed change to Backstab positioning. Reworked itemization is the real variable — Classic dagger BiS will not survive the loot pass.

foreverDates.label: Beta
foreverDates.note: Live now — testing runs through 21 Oct

foreverChanges.title: Rogues can use One-Handed Axes
foreverChanges.body: Axes join Daggers, Swords, Maces, Fist Weapons, Bows, Crossbows and Thrown on the Rogue weapon list. It is the single clearest mechanical addition to the class so far.
foreverChanges.impact: One more weapon type competing for your main hand, and one more weapon skill to cap if you commit to it.

foreverChanges.title: Each spec gets a sharper identity
foreverChanges.body: Assassination is being pointed at poison damage, Subtlety at bleeds and stealth effects, and Combat keeps its straightforward upfront style.
foreverChanges.impact: The Classic answer — "play Combat Swords" — stops being automatic. Assassination and Subtlety are getting actual design attention for the first time.

foreverChanges.title: Hit and Crit are unified — including poisons
foreverChanges.body: Spell, melee and ranged hit collapse into one Hit stat, and the same happens to crit. Blizzard's BlizzCon deep dive named Rogues directly, saying the change "helps hybrid specializations such as Retribution Paladins and Enhancement Shaman, while also letting Warriors, Hunters, and Rogues benefit when improving the reliability of tools such as Taunts, Poisons, and Traps." The worked example was Lionheart Helm: +18 Strength, 2% hit and 2% crit applying everywhere.
foreverChanges.impact: Your gear no longer has dead stats on it, and your poison applications stop living on a separate table from your swings.

foreverChanges.title: Weapon Skill survives, but tuned down per item
foreverChanges.body: Blizzard's own wording from the deep dive: "Weapon skill still works as it always has, but items with weapon skill offer less of it per item so they are not always the obvious best choice."
foreverChanges.impact: Still cap your weapon skill. Do not expect one item to do half the job for you the way a couple of Classic pieces did.

foreverChanges.title: Itemization is being deliberately "unsolved"
foreverChanges.body: Every dungeon boss has had its loot reviewed. Quests, world drops, professions and existing items are all being updated, with hundreds of new or adjusted drops and some effects tied to specific environments or creature types.
foreverChanges.impact: Do not build a Forever BiS list from Classic Era data. It will be wrong, and confidently wrong is worse than empty.

foreverChanges.title: Talent trees keep their shape, lose their certainties
foreverChanges.body: Three Classic-style trees, 51 points, but individual talents are redesigned and there is a new 16-point milestone to plan around.
foreverChanges.impact: Every talent split on this page is a Classic Era build. Treat them as history from 4 November onward.

foreverChanges.title: Slower, more tactical combat
foreverChanges.body: Blizzard framed the combat goals as keeping classes simple and distinct, with slower pacing and group play where crowd control and threat genuinely matter.
foreverChanges.impact: Sap, Kick, Blind and Gouge stop being things you forgot you had. Rogue utility is priced in rather than tolerated.

foreverChanges.title: Mutilate for Assassination
foreverChanges.body: A dual-wield strike generating multiple combo points was shown on the Assassination tree in the playable BlizzCon demo. This is community capture, not a published Blizzard ability page.
foreverChanges.impact: Promising, unconfirmed, and subject to change before launch. Do not plan a build around it yet.

foreverChanges.title: Skyborne can be Rogues
foreverChanges.body: The new Skyborne race can play Rogue on both Alliance and Horde. Their racial toolkit includes a glide that lets them float safely down from height. Race access requires the Heroic Pack or higher.
foreverChanges.impact: A new racial spread to compare against Human sword skill, Orc stun resist and Night Elf stealth. Nobody has numbers yet.

foreverChanges.title: Ability-by-ability Rogue breakdown
foreverChanges.body: Blizzard has published a full rework preview for Paladin and covered general systems affecting Rogues — Hit/Crit, Weapon Skill — in the BlizzCon deep dive. It still has not published a dedicated ability-by-ability breakdown for Rogue, and today's live Q&A did not add one.
foreverChanges.impact: Anything you read claiming a specific Forever Rogue rotation is either your own beta testing or still guessing. Trust the beta client over secondhand claims.

foreverChanges.title: Raid and dungeon lineup is confirmed
foreverChanges.body: Blizzard's What's Next panel named the launch content: two raids — Hyjal Summit (20-player) and Barrow Deeps (10-player) — plus nine dungeons including Hall of Thanes, Ruins of Lordaeron and City of Dalaran, new zones Mount Hyjal, Shen'dralas and Riverglades, the Skyborne starting zone Zephras Isle, and a 15v15 PvP battleground, Darkspear Islands.
foreverChanges.impact: Names and counts are locked in, but encounter mechanics and loot tables are not. The raid notes on this page are still Classic Era tiers until beta testing produces real Forever strats.

foreverChanges.title: Beta is live
foreverChanges.body: The Forever beta opened today, 17 September, right after the live developer Q&A. Opening-week access covers the Skyborne race and Zephras Isle zone, an initial level cap of 20 (raised to 30 later in the test), and two dungeons — Hall of Thanes and Ruins of Lordaeron. Testing runs through 21 October.
foreverChanges.impact: You can play a Rogue in Forever right now instead of only reading about it — just at a low level cap. Nothing past the opening test content is accessible yet.

faqs.a: No. Poisons do not scale with Spell Power in Classic. The only place Spell Power touches a Rogue is Dragonbreath Chili, which is a curiosity for people chasing the last fraction of a percent. What does change in Forever: Blizzard confirmed the unified Hit stat covers every attack including poisons, so your hit rating will feed poison applications in a way it does not today.

Yes. Instant Poison and Deadly Poison damage both scale with your Attack Power — confirmed by a dev on the Rogue Classic Discord. It is not a huge chunk of the total, but it is real, and it is one more reason a Rogue stacking Attack Power sees it show up everywhere on the damage meter, not just in white swings.

faqs.q: What has Blizzard actually confirmed for Rogues in Forever?
faqs.a: Three things, concretely. Rogues can use One-Handed Axes. Each spec is getting a sharper identity — Assassination toward poison damage, Subtlety toward bleeds and stealth, Combat staying upfront. And the talent trees keep their Classic shape while individual talents are redesigned around a new 16-point milestone. Mutilate appeared on the Assassination tree in the BlizzCon demo, but that is community capture from playable footage, not a published ability. Blizzard has published a full ability-by-ability rework preview for Paladin and has not yet done the same for Rogue.

faqs.q: How does unified Hit and Crit change my gearing?
faqs.a: It removes the dead stats. In Classic, spell hit on a piece of gear is worthless to you and melee hit is worthless to a Mage. In Forever there is one Hit stat and one Crit stat covering every attack a character makes. Blizzard’s worked example was Lionheart Helm — plus 18 Strength, 2% hit and 2% crit, all of it applying to everything. The practical effect for you is that more items become plausible, and fewer of them are obviously other people’s loot.

faqs.q: Should I build a Forever BiS list now?
faqs.a: No, and you should be suspicious of anyone who has. Blizzard has reviewed the loot on every dungeon boss and is updating quests, world drops, professions and existing items, with hundreds of new or adjusted drops and some effects tied to specific environments or creature types. The stated goal is to "unsolve" Classic. A Classic Era BiS list ported to Forever will be confidently wrong, which is worse than being empty.

leveling.name: Combat Swords
leveling.body: The path of least resistance. Sinister Strike, Slice and Dice, Eviscerate, no positioning to think about. You arrive at 60 already knowing your raid rotation.

leveling.name: Daggers & stealth
leveling.body: Ambush openers, fewer fights taken, more fights won outright. Slower to gear, faster to move, and considerably more fun if you like picking your battles.

changelog.text: Stood up the first iteration of the WoW Forever Rogue Handbook — spec board, talents, poisons, rotation, gear, consumables and the Forever watch, all in one place.
Warcraft Forever announced at BlizzCon. Beta 17 September, launch 4 November, level cap staying at 60. Rogues confirmed to gain One-Handed Axes.
